reviewed.script: integrations/puredarwin/m1-dart-survey/darwin-dart-survey-test 0f1c4ab9d1431eb2 (diff base: approved and qualified darwin-native-startup-test dcba72de)

verdict: APPROVE the supervisor structure. The binding is conditional on the final collector (/usr/bin/darwin-dart-survey) being reviewed against the requirements below before packet assembly. The only change is one block inserted after nonce validation and before the original DL12_NATIVE_BEGIN. The qualified native-only startup, GUI and closed-cleanup path follows unchanged.
diff: Inserted after line 6 (the nonce length check): a comment; 'DL13_DART_BEGIN_<n> register_writes=0 device_initialization=false'; 'survey_rc=0; if /usr/bin/darwin-dart-survey --nonce "$nonce"; then :; else survey_rc=$?; fi'; 'DL13_DART_COLLECTED_<n> rc=<raw rc> initialization_proven=false'; 'case "$survey_rc" in 0|77) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac'.

Everything from DL12_NATIVE_BEGIN onward is byte-identical to dcba72de (inventory gate, keyboard-node wait, mouse refusal, keyboard-only compositor, finite 80 s observer, closed 6-record export, compositor TERM/wait, STATUS, footer and return).
verified: set -eu safety: the collector runs inside if/else, so a non-zero rc does not trip errexit, and the raw rc is printed before any decision. One invocation; no loop or retry.

Fail-closed: any rc other than 0 or 77 (crash, usage error, missing or malformed diagnostic, if the collector maps those so) exits 1 before the runtime directory, the cleanup trap, the compositor or the client exist, so nothing needs cleanup. Root's controller still performs the mandatory reset and Linux recovery.

Refusal preserved: rc 77 continues to the desktop, so a kernel-recorded refusal (NOT_READY/UNSUPPORTED/...) is kept as an observation and the finite GUI/cleanup is still exercised. The DL13_DART_COLLECTED rc line is the survey verdict; the later STATUS/footer never imply a survey result.
No input or write paths are added. The host stays sealed after the launcher (09cd/25694c88 native mode), and the script writes nothing to registers, HID nodes or the PTY.
collector_requirements_before_packet: Read-only IORegistry access only (an IOResources property read). No IOServiceOpen or user client, no MMIO, no device-tree writes, no retries beyond a single bounded read.

Exact validation: OSData length 764, version 1, sample_count <= 88, reads_attempted <= 1024, failure_region <= 5, result in {0,1,2,-1,-2,-3,-4}. For result 0 also require sample_count 88, reads 889, region 5 and offset 0. Read both the provider copy (PDDARTSurveyDiagnosticV1 on IOResources) and, if present, the instance copy; when both exist, require them byte-equal.

Exit-code mapping: 0 only for a well-formed result 0; 77 only for a well-formed kernel-recorded refusal (result != 0); any other code for a missing property, wrong length or version, inconsistent counts or a read error. A missing diagnostic must never become 0 or 77.

Evidence: print the full 764 raw bytes once, nonce-bound, as chunked hex with a SHA-256 (as the terminal records collector does), so the saved console preserves the diagnostic independently of the GUI run. Values include firmware table physical addresses and must stay private capture.

Bounded output and runtime well inside the existing 180 s host plan: launch at +78 s, collector about 1 s, then the unchanged 80 s observer and closed export, which finished at +160 s in native startup001.
qualification_notes: Survey qualification rests on the decoded raw bytes in the console, together with the kernel IOLog 'PDDARTSurvey: result=... diagnostic_copy=1 provider_preserved=1 instance_recorded=...'. Neither the marker alone nor the GUI footer is enough.
Even result 0 is a noncoherent read sequence (README): no translation, ownership or initialization claim.
scope: Read-only script diff and record review. No hardware, builds or edits.
